There are multiple endings to GTA 6 , and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed. 

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission , but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

GTA 6 endings on the bridge In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. items.title: The Grand Theft Auto 6 hacker who was hospitalized in 2023 has been released on parole with a warning not to do it again
items.summary:
A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.

Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord.

"Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated. 

"Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from."
Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft , Samsung , Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals. 

But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room…

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 creative director says he's suffering from 'GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression,' jokes that 'Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled'
items.summary:
It's been a big week for videogames—or rather, videogame. Grand Theft Auto 6 is enjoying what may very well be the single greatest media launch in history, securing over $3.7 billion in launch sales. But as Rockstar enjoys its acclaim, other developers—like Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski—are professing some anxiety about releasing their own games in a post-GTA 6 world.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled."

(Image credit: Igor Sarzynski, Anna Megill on Bluesky) That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—"

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

In Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion .

In a follow-up post , Sarzynski acknowledged that each project is doing its own thing, while noting that GTA 6's example will benefit other game developers by serving…

I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.

"Fixed an issue that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. items.title: Players Have Found a GTA 6 60fps Glitch, but It Just Reaffirms Rockstar's 30fps Cap
items.summary:
One of GTA 6 's biggest controversies was Rockstar's decision to keep the game's framerate locked at 30fps , rather than allowing for an unlocked mode. Over the weekend, players managed to find a glitch on Xbox Series X that lets you unlock the frame rate, albeit to mixed results. 

The glitch is performed by booting up the game when the Xbox console is set to 60fps, then going into the console settings, switching the system to 120fps, launching another game, and then using Quick Resume to start GTA 6 back up. That process essentially tricks the system into unlocking the frame rate, and some people have been able to push it a bit higher than the game's default 30fps lock. 

The folks over at Digital Foundry were able to put the '60fps glitch' to the test, though, and found that while you could push upwards of 60fps, it was limited to situations where, "If you look straight up in the ocean, frame-rates can just about graze 60fps." 

Instead, Digital Foundry's results reaffirm Rockstar's decision to ship the game with a 30fps lock. While the game managed an average of 36fps in the first hour of the game, GTA 6 only gets more demanding as it progresses into Vice City, where NPCs and explosions are both more prevalent. And, in those situations, the game still has sharp drops to lower frame rates. 

The whole reason a 30fps cap makes sense for GTA 6 is consistency. While this glitch shows that the game sometimes has the headroom to peek above 30fps, and even into the 40s, getting rid of the cap would just mean the difference between the peaks and valleys of the frame rate would…

items.title: YouTuber Discovers Wild GTA 6 Easter Egg, Cracks Code in Just 3 Days to Reveal Brilliant Surprise

A YouTuber has uncovered the wildest GTA 6 Easter egg yet. Following a series of arcane clues and pulling a set of switches in the correct order sees players transported back to the 1980s.

Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow. 

The Easter egg begins in the R&D tower in Key Lento, GTA 6’s starting area, but spans almost the entire map. Players have to pull a series of switches and press certain buttons to trigger a portal into the past, complete with new voice acting from Danny Dyer as Kent Paul. 

After scaling the tower, the YouTuber ( Memeio ) noticed that a sound effect from GTA Vice City plays when he messed with the lever and button. A poster for LPL (Leonida Power and Light) in the room then guided him around Leonida to the LPL power substations dotted around the map. 

Each substation contained letters written on its walls. Memeio was so committed to figuring out the mystery that he actually followed the power cables across the map to track them all down. 

After putting all the letters together from all 12 substations, Memeio realized they spelled out an interesting phrase: “Life is passing me by.” That phrase was a cheat code in Vice City that sped up the in-game clock. 

On PlayStation, the code for that cheat was: Circle, L1, Square, L1, Square, L1, Triangle, Circle, Triangle.

Barely a week ago I wrote that "I suspect a cross-section of [Queen's Domain's] goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art". Well, I was right. Here it is and it looks rad as hell.

No, really. Even if you're not a Queen's Domain player—or maybe especially if you're not—take a look at this thing. (Image credit: Rockstar) Deciding whether to take the cut or pure drugs in GTA 6 is a decision you'll make during the Dealer's Choice mission in Chapter 3. 

The proposal is that if you can pass off the drugs cut with baby powder, you can keep the profit, but the deal might go south if they realise, while bringing the pure stuff should make the dealers happy. Here's what happens if you choose either:

Cut drugs : If you choose the cut drugs, the dealers will immediately realise the stuff is cut with baby powder. They'll confront you, at which point you can either offer to give them half off (which reduces your profit to the same as it would have been if you'd taken pure), or you can tell them to take it or leave it. This second option will cause a gunfight, but assuming you survive, you can grab the money from their car and make maximum profit. This also doesn't have any other consequences. Pure drugs : If you choose this option, you'll make less money, but the deal will go off without a hitch after they test it. That means no gunfights. With that in mind, I'd say the cut drugs are the best to pick. You get maximum profit, a cool shootout that makes the mission less boring, and it doesn't have any significant consequences afterwards.

In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered , thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. items.title: GTA's treatment of women 'has not been good', says Rockstar vet delighted by 'long overdue' female protagonist in GTA 6
items.summary:
Lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

That vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens , GTA OG Brian Baglow said he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

Baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built". 

That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".

Baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an important series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted…

Yet there was no AI disclosure on the DLC's Steam page.

Players were not thrilled by this development. Steam user reviews on The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ dropped to Overwhelmingly Negative, with only 8% positive recent reviews. Players put the blame on Nicalis, who licence Binding of Isaac from its original creator Edmund McMillen. "Edmund please take back control of the game", one said.

"Woke up to a shit show," McMillen wrote on the hatesite formerly known as Twitter when he found out what had happened, "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."

As of the latest update, the AI-generated music is gone. "It's a little sad given Joey Kuras (game's sound designer) did some excellent sounds for Mewgenics", ShweetStuff wrote, "but I suppose this is the industry nowadays!"

items.title: Nvidia released a hotfix for its driver hammering your SSD, but it doesn't actually work
items.summary:
Over the last couple of weeks, some Nvidia users noticed their SSDs were taking a hammering , reporting their driver's log file was being overwritten constantly, sometimes to the tune of 30 GB every hour. Which obviously isn't great for the lifespan of the valuable SSD you've got it installed on.

Given the problem was caused by recent driver updates, rolling back to version 621.01 was the best solution until Nvidia could do something about it. Which they did, releasing a hotfix as version 621.35 . It's not available in the GeForce app yet, but you can download it directly from Nvidia's site. Not that you should.

As users on the Nvidia subreddit are reporting, the problem persists. While the hotfix reduces the peak write rate and prevents it for a short while after reboot, it eventually creeps back in. One user reported that overnight the log file was still being rewritten by approximately 4.5 GB every hour.

So yeah, the best solution remains to roll back to version 621.01 and, as always with Nvidia drivers, to hold off on updating to the latest driver until it's been confirmed safe. If this ongoing saga sounds familiar, it's because the same thing happened to AMD's GPU drivers earlier this month. Maybe vibecoding driver updates and then vibecoding fixes for their inevitable bugs isn't the best way of doing things.
items.t: Nvidia released a hotfix for its driver hammering your SSD, but it doesn't actually work

items.title: Unreal Engine 6 to jettison key scripting feature earlier than planned in favor of AI coding
items.summary:
Unreal Engine 6 will not launch with the engine's long-standard Blueprints scripting system. The news came in a Friday, November 19 post on the Unreal Engine website , written by Epic Games executive vice president of development, Marcus Wassmer. Here's Wassmer's top-level summary from the post:

Blueprints have not (and it appears, will not) be deprecated in Unreal Engine 5, and the company maintains that projects will still be easy to convert from UE5 to UE6. Wassmer cited a declining cost in AI task completion as one reason for this belief, as well as the team's ongoing, but apparently successful conversion of Fortnite's Blueprint library to UE6's Verse programming language through an AI-assisted process.

Blueprints are a widely-used feature of Unreal. Former Valve developer Chet Faliszek, an AI skeptic, has put out a vlog on the subject . Essentially, Faliszek argues that Blueprints (and features like them in other game engines) represent a middle ground between artistic and technical work, an introduction and skill builder for less technically-minded developers. Without them, such developers seemingly have to either learn Verse code, or integrate LLM prompting into their workflows.

"We made a new skill in the middle there, between normal and expert," Faliszek said of intermediate tools like Blueprints. items.title: GTA 6 needed a dedicated team to make sure all its different body types could share animations: 'It was a huge team effort'

In an interview with IGN , Rockstar vice president of animation Mark Tennant said it was an early decision in development to "push the variation in character sizes and body types … This required us to establish a very robust way to share animations between characters while still resolving multiple points of contact, such as most vehicle interactions and grappling in hand-to-hand combat."

It also took eschewing a "traditional approach" in favor of "new techniques," the sort I imagine you can only implement at Rockstar levels of budget and manpower. items.title: New Dota 2 patch tries to help games end faster, adds an item that summons super creeps in every lane at once
items.summary:
The longest game of Dota I've played was comfortably past the 70-minute mark. Matches that gloriously long-winded can be fun in small doses, but they can also be exhausting and infuriating—this is Dota we're talking about, after all. The latest patch to rearrange the venerable MOBA, 7.42, is finally here , and it's got tons of changes that might just prevent your games from going feature length.

The most exciting of these, for my money, is the Greater Horn of Battle: a guaranteed drop from the Tormentor neutral monster that summons a wave of super creeps in all your team's lanes (the patch notes refer to them as the more powerful mega creeps, but players have noted the stats don't match up that way). If you've played League of Legends or Deadlock, it fills a niche similar to the Rift Herald or Deadlock's Unstable Rifts—an objective you can complete in the earlier stages of a game to push lane(s) hard.

It's an ability that, if timed correctly, could force the other team to scramble to protect each lane or risk losing lots of ground. And it's not the only change with the potential to speed up matches. 

Base hero health has gone up from 120 to 200, with the caveat that strength now gives less health per point, meaning that heroes will be sturdier early on but slightly squishier later. The Glyph of Fortification, a teamwide spell that makes buildings invulnerable, no longer resets its cooldown when certain buildings go down. Heroes also now gain experience passively, even when dead, meaning that you never completely stop growing stronger as the match progresses.
